Latino residential concentration in California places, 2010 and 2020

Source: R/data.R
ca_place_concentration.Rd

Block-based measures of how concentrated the Hispanic or Latino population is within every California place (incorporated places and census designated places), for the 2010 and 2020 censuses and for the total and voting-age populations. Built with seg_blocks(), seg_measures() and seg_clusters() by data-raw/ca_place_concentration.R in the package source.

Usage

ca_place_concentration

Format

A tibble with one row per place, year and universe:

place_geoid

Seven-digit place code: state FIPS code 06 and the place FIPS code.

place_name

Census place name, such as "Palmdale city, California".

year

Census year, 2010 or 2020.

universe

"total" for the whole population or "vap" for the voting-age population (18 and over).

n_blocks

Number of census blocks in the place.

pop_total, pop_group

Population and Hispanic or Latino population, summed over blocks.

group_share

Hispanic or Latino share of the population.

dissimilarity, isolation, exposure

Block-level segregation measures of Latinos against everyone else; see seg_measures().

majority_share

Share of Latinos living in majority-Latino blocks.

n_clusters

Number of contiguous clusters of majority-Latino blocks.

largest_pop, largest_group, largest_share

Population, Latino population and Latino share of the largest cluster.

n_districts

Council size assumed: 5.

ideal_pop

pop_total / n_districts.

largest_ratio

largest_pop / ideal_pop; NaN for the few places with no population.

n_viable

Clusters with at least ideal_pop people.

n_districts_floor

Sum over clusters of whole ideal districts, a heuristic count of majority-Latino districts; see seg_clusters().

Source

U.S. Census Bureau: 2010 Census Summary File 1 (tables P4 and P11) and 2020 Census Redistricting Data (P.L. 94-171, tables P2 and P4), through the Census API; Block Assignment Files for places; TIGER/Line block shapefiles. These are U.S. government works in the public domain.

Details

For voting rights work use universe == "vap". Courts look at citizen voting-age population, which is not published for blocks, so the voting-age population is the closest block-level count.

The district columns assume a five-district council, with seg_clusters() defaults: majority means above 50 percent, rook contiguity, and empty blocks may bridge clusters. For another council size k, largest_pop / (pop_total / k) gives the largest cluster in ideal districts. n_viable and n_districts_floor need every cluster's population, so recompute them with seg_clusters().
